instruction: Buy me a dish rack from my amazon wishlist that will fit in my kitchen countertop of 15.3X13.3 (LxW) inches.
notes: Single-app task (amazon) plus supervisor. The wish list is modeled with two dish-rack products; static init facts (dish-rack, fits-countertop) encode the ground truth that only one has length <= 15.3 and width <= 13.3, while knowledge predicates (wish-list-shown, dimensions-known) force the agent to list the wish list and inspect the product before selecting it. add_product_to_cart is called with clear_cart_first=true (flag object) so the resulting order contains exactly one item, matching the evaluation (CartEntry changes are ignored). Payment card and address ids are discovered via show_payment_cards / show_addresses (no address is added/updated, as required). place_order asserts the nullary goal predicate fitting-dish-rack-ordered only when the cart holds a fitting wish-list dish rack; supervisor-complete-task is gated on it and is the final step. The reference solution has 10 calls (likely one extra show_product on the non-fitting candidate); the optimal PDDL plan has 9 steps since the planner inspects only the fitting product, but the agent may inspect every wish-list dish rack at runtime.
